title: Add Edges to Make Degrees of All Nodes Even
summary: Given an undirected graph with n nodes numbered 1 to n, and a 2D array of edges, determine if adding at most two edges (without creating self-loops or duplicates) can make the degree of each node even.
statement: Given an undirected graph with n nodes numbered 1 to n, and a 2D array of edges, determine if adding at most two edges (without creating self-loops or duplicates) can make the degree of each node even. Return true if possible, otherwise false.
constraints: The graph is simple and undirected on nodes 1 through n.
Add zero, one, or two new edges without self-loops or duplicate existing edges.
Return whether every node can have even degree.
hints: Only odd-degree nodes need parity changes, and each added edge toggles exactly two endpoints.
Zero odds already succeeds; two odds need their direct missing edge or a shared intermediate node.
Four odds require one of the three pairings to consist of two missing edges.
More than four odds cannot be fixed by two edges, while these enumerated cases cover every possible parity toggle pattern.
editorial: More than four odds cannot be fixed by two edges, while these enumerated cases cover every possible parity toggle pattern.

tests.explanation: The odd-degree nodes can be paired by valid missing edges using at most two additions.
Four odd nodes exist, but the required pairings among them are already edges, so two legal additions cannot fix all degrees.
